plain_english: When you see someone else in a position of power, remember that you don't want power anyway. When you see someone else who's rich, think about what you have instead of riches. If you have nothing to replace them with, then you're miserable. But if you don't want riches in the first place, know that you have more than that rich person — and what you have is worth much more.
original_excerpt: When you see another man in the possession of power (magistracy), set against this the fact that you have not the want (desire) of power; when you see another rich, see what you possess in place of riches: for if you possess nothing in place of them, you are miserable; but if you have not the want of riches, know that you possess more than this man possesses and what is worth much more.
source_reference: Discourses, To a Person Who Had Been Changed to a Character of Shamelessness, Section 1
